toolCallDetails.arguments: {"path":"neuron_growth_openai-gpt-6-sol_01.html","edit_description":"Create a complete standalone HTML5 document in this new file (only external dependency is a single CDN script for dat.gui 0.7.9; all HTML/CSS/JS inline, no other assets/libraries). Build a polished futuristic neon animated neuron-growth simulation in exactly one <canvas width=\"800\" height=\"800\"> centered on dark #05070f page; responsive CSS scales canvas visually without changing its intrinsic 800x800 pixels. Exact default colors #05070f background, #101a3a inner glow, #00e5ff main branches, #d6ff00 accent branches, #ff2bd6 synapses, #fff36a electric pulses, #ffd400 UI. Draw ambient radial gradient, subtle procedural grid/scanline with canvas only, faint vignette. Use canvas shadowBlur for restrained bloom. Add tasteful title/readout and decorative labels using CSS/canvas (no extra canvas). Include short comments demarcating setup, GUI setup, neuron growth, synapse detection, pulse animation and rendering; no references to games, movies, brands or copyrighted visual styles in code/comments (the required dat.gui library name is fine).\nImplement lightweight requestAnimationFrame simulation using dt capped for tab switching, pause/resume, clear canvas (clear resets arrays, ceases generation and keeps drawing empty background; regenerate starts growth). 3–6 random seed neurons near center chosen via GUI neuronCount default 4 (integer slider 3..6); seed nuclei drawn. For each seed spawn several diverging branch roots; each branch has neuron index, parent pointer, depth, direction, randomized thickness, max length and points array, active tip, progresses a small amount each frame according to growthSpeed in pixels/second; smooth organic branches via small direction drift bounded by curvature and rendered using quadraticCurveTo over midpoint or equivalent; occasional small side branches and splitting when branch completes; enforce branch max depth and global max branch count ~230 and boundary margin; branches finish when maximum length or boundary is reached; stop growing once active list empty or cap reached, without endlessly respawning. Ensure event probabilities are per branch completion, not per frame, and ensure active list update handles additions without missing/removing them. Synapses only between tips from DIFFERENT neuron branches within adjustable distance, reject duplicate branch pair and reject near-duplicate connections nearby, cap ~100; check every 0.2 seconds and again after growth stops; allow tips of completed branches and possibly growing branches but store stable endpoint positions for links; glow synapse and animated breathing. Pulse generation periodically at GUI frequency even after growth, choose random synapse; animate a tiny bright moving spark smoothly along short inter-neuron synapse via linear interpolation, optionally use route sampling of ancestry for path travel, cap active pulse array ~24, dt-driven speed and brightness, render small spark with shadowBlur. For reliable activity after growth, choose a reasonable default threshold 35-50 and dense interconnected central branches; if there are no links scene should still breathe naturally, but do not fabricate connections beyond threshold.\nCreate dat.gui controls arranged exact folders Growth, Synapses, Pulses, Visuals. Growth: neuron count, branch growth speed, max branch depth, branch split chance, branch curvature, max branch length. Synapses: distance threshold, glow strength. Pulses: speed, frequency, brightness. Visuals: addColor background color, branch color, accent branch color, synapse color, pulse color. Buttons regenerate network, clear canvas, pause/resume animation (display labels readable, toggle paused and update label or dynamic button name). Changes affecting topology regenerate onFinishChange; speed/color/glow/brightness/frequency live; threshold change recomputes links and resets pulses. Add concise helpful GUI labels. Keep code compact/simple, arrays/objects only, stable performance. Include unobtrusive CSS styling for dat.gui and screen layout with panel visible on desktop, not obscuring canvas on small displays."}
